networkPolicy.desc: AdMob and Google's web ad hosts are blocked; the forecast site stays open

policies.notes:
Written from the binary. The application is a WebView on https://m.weather2day.co.il/ with push registration at www.weather2day.co.il/push.php; both stay open. AdMob is the in-app advertising: banners, interstitials, rewarded and native ads (35 references to the native ad classes, which render pictures). Those hosts and Google's web ad serving hosts (securepubads, googletagservices) are blocked, and are listed here even though the global list carries most of them, because app builds that predate globalBlockedHosts only read this.

What this cannot see: the ads the site itself serves. The page was fetched for this policy from a NetFree line, which strips ad scripts and injects its own, so the copy read here showed no third party ad host at all. An ad network the site uses that is not Google's would show up on a device off NetFree, through the tunnel, as a host to add here. The site also sells a premium subscription that removes ads.

Not yet watched on a device through the tunnel.

networkPolicy.desc: Navigation works; place photos, attraction thumbnails and Street View do not

policies.notes:
Every host is written out, and that is the whole point of this file. Upstream blocks "*.googleusercontent.com", which reads as a wildcard and is not one: in this data format the star is dropped and a www twin added, so it expands to googleusercontent.com and www.googleusercontent.com and matches nothing that serves a photograph. See KDroidHosts in the application for the evidence.

The numbered families are written out in full, 0 through 9, because the device proved that guessing the range is how photographs get through. A first pass covered lh3 through lh6 and the photographs kept arriving; the log said why:

    lh3.googleusercontent.com -> 0.0.0.0
    gz0.googleusercontent.com -> 216.239.38.135

gz0 was not on the list and was serving them. Listing a range that does not exist yet costs nothing; leaving one out costs the whole rule.

Note that gz0.googleusercontent.com answers on the same address as mobilemaps-pa-gz.googleapis.com, which carries the map itself. That is why this file blocks names and never addresses: the map keeps working, the photographs do not.

encrypted-tbn0.gstatic.com was found serving the photographs in the attractions tab (seen on a device, 2026-10-20). It is Google's image thumbnail host, the same one image search uses, and nothing the map needs; the family is written out 0 through 9 for the reason above.

NAVIGATION_AND_MAIL_ONLY.desc: Mail only; Google Chat, Spaces and Meet are blocked

REDUCED_RISK.desc: Mail only; Google Chat, Spaces and Meet are blocked

policies.notes:
Chat is blocked in every mode, which is a deliberate divergence from upstream. Upstream defines the block for NAVIGATION_AND_MAIL_ONLY only and opens Gmail completely from REDUCED_RISK up; since a policy inherits downward, that left Chat reachable in REDUCED_RISK and in MOST_OPEN, which is the mode most devices run in. Upstream also ships the host list as the literal placeholder "HOST OF GOOGLE CHAT", so there was nothing to copy: the hosts here were written for this catalog.

hangouts.googleapis.com is the one that matters and it was missing. chat.google.com alone blocks the web front end and leaves the backend the application actually talks to, which is still the Hangouts API: Chat kept its old service name when it was renamed. tools/extract_hosts.py on the Gmail APK on the device is where this came from, along with its staging twins (autopush-, preprod-, loadtest-, daily-) which are not listed here because a shipped build does not dial them.

"*.googlevideo.com" used to be on this list and has been removed. It reads as a wildcard and is not one: in this data format the star is dropped and a www twin added, so it expanded to googlevideo.com and www.googlevideo.com and blocked nothing that carries video. Leaving it in was worse than leaving it out, because it read like a rule that was working.

What this cannot reach: the notification. A new message in a Space still raises a banner, because that push arrives over the connection Google Play Services keeps open for every application on the device, not over any connection of Gmail's. Blocking it would silence every notification on the device. The message itself does not load, which is what a host rule can do here.

networkPolicy.desc: Google search and the forum links are blocked; transcription and updates stay open

policies.notes:
Written from the binary. classes.dex carries https://www.google.com/search?q= for its spoken Google search, https://www.google.com/ and search?q=a which read as a reachability probe for that feature, and two support threads, mitmachim.top/post/1249818 and rechavimzelaze.ovh/post/156187. There is no WebView in the application: search and the threads are handed to the browser with ACTION_VIEW, so they also fail wherever the browser has no network. They are blocked here so that does not depend on the browser, and so the probe fails and the application can report the search as blocked instead of offering a button that does nothing.

Open on purpose: api.groq.com, which is the transcription itself, and raw.githubusercontent.com, api.github.com and cdn.jsdelivr.net, which are its update check and the APK download. waze.com/ul is a link handed to Waze. ogenplay.com is its store page link.

The application also has its own password lock for Google search, which survives a reinstall. That is a setting inside the application, not something this policy can turn on.

Not yet watched on a device through the tunnel.

Upstream's name for the Home Front Command application. No package by this name was found on a device; the application that is installed is com.alert.meserhadash, and it carries the certificate whose SHA-1 upstream records here. Kept in case a TV build exists under this name and shares the signer. A policy for a package nobody has is inert, so it costs nothing.

Open on purpose: a Haredi Torah application, and video could not be separated from audio by host.

Watched on a device: the API runs over clear HTTP on streaming.kolhalashon.com (the base URL is chosen at runtime; www.kolhalashon.com and kol.kolhl.com are in the code too), iPhone/GetMediaURL.aspx?FileID=N&FileType=audio|video answers audio with an https URL under /mp3/ and video with an http URL under /mp4/, both on www.kolhalashon.com. Live plays in a WebView with JW Player (ssl.p.jwpcdn.com, prd.jwpltx.com) from streaming.kolhalashon.com:443; older live streams use port 1935 for audio and video alike. A video only block would need a rule on the clear HTTP path, which the filter does not do.

Open on purpose: a Haredi Torah application, and video could not be separated from audio by host.

A WebView over www.kolhalashon.com/he/regularSite/home/app (the binary also carries home/appNoVideo, which a policy cannot force). Its pages pull from www.kolhalashon.com, chatrace.com, static.cloudflareinsights.com, www.googletagmanager.com and accounts.google.com. Both audio and video are served from media-cdn.kolhalashon.com over https (api/files/GetPlayToken/N/1 is mp3, /2 to /4 are mp4), so a host rule would take audio down with video.

policies.notes:

What it needs: api.noeg.co.il (a Parse server), noeg.co.il (app data, sign in, password reset, friend sync), book.noeg.co.il and teo.co.il (lessons and teachers), and Firebase (remote config, Crashlytics).

networkPolicy.desc: Its own backend and the vehicle register, and nothing else

policies.notes:
An allow list rather than a block list, because this application needs two hosts and naming them is easier than naming everything it does not need.

The list was written from the binary and corrected by the device, and the difference between the two is the point. tools/extract_hosts.py found data.gov.il, the government open data portal that holds the vehicle register, and that is the host the application is about. It is not the host it dials. Watching it run said so on the first launch:

    Flow blocked: uid=10261 dst=213.137.85.57:443
    host=scan-car.xyz (WHITELIST_MISS)

scan-car.xyz is the developer's own backend, which queries the register on the application's behalf and appears nowhere in the strings the extractor can reach. Static extraction narrows the search; only the device closes it. data.gov.il is kept because a later version may go direct, and a host that is never dialled costs nothing.

classic-assets.eascdn.net is deliberately absent. It is the Expo update channel, and it would let the application replace its own code after review without the store or this catalog seeing the change. The application runs on the bundle it shipped with.
Tzeva Adom alerts. Unfiltered for the same reason as the Home Front Command application beside it.

networkPolicy.desc: Facebook sign in and tracking are blocked; everything else stays open

policies.notes:
Written from the binary. What it needs: gravez.me, backendapi.gravez.me and services.gravez.me (search, route markers, the paid services page), apiendusers.corido.co.il and contentpages.corido.co.il (the vendor's API and content pages such as Prayers.html), coridopersonalimages.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com (photos users upload to a deceased's page, left open on purpose) and Firebase (auth, messaging, Crashlytics, Analytics). The map comes from OpenStreetMap extracts bundled in assets, so no tile host is needed.

Blocked: the Facebook SDK, which is there for sign in, sharing and app events. Its host is built at runtime as graph.%s, which is why the extractor did not list graph.facebook.com. WhatsApp, Telegram and Facebook share links are handed to those applications and are not this application's traffic.

Not an allow list on purpose: several backends, and a list that misses one breaks a screen without saying why. Not yet watched on a device through the tunnel.

networkPolicy.desc: Marketing push, attribution and Facebook are blocked; the application itself stays open

policies.notes:
Written from the binary. What it needs: ten.inmanage.com, its API, banners and coupons alike, and hotclient5.inmanage.com, the one domain in its network security configuration. Firebase for Crashlytics and dynamic links (tenapp.page.link).

Blocked: Pushwoosh, which delivers its marketing push notifications, so promotional pushes with pictures stop arriving; AppsFlyer, which is install attribution and marketing tracking; and the Facebook SDK. The AppsFlyer and Facebook names are assembled at runtime from format strings ("%sinapps.%s", "graph.%s" and so on), which is why the extractor did not list most of them; the list here is those strings filled in with appsflyersdk.com and facebook.com.

What this cannot do: the in-app banners come from ten.inmanage.com, the same host as the fuelling itself. That is why the catalog entry carries hasUnmodestImage.

Not yet watched on a device through the tunnel. If the banner images turn out to come from a separate image host, that host is the one to add here.

Blocked: the Vimeo player and CDN, which carry the full screen advertising videos behind What's New (seen: player.vimeo.com, download-video-ak.vimeocdn.com), AppsFlyer under the tocqqo prefix, Emarsys marketing (its inbox, events and recommender), the Facebook SDK and New Relic. networkPolicy.desc: Tag Manager, YouTube, Facebook and imgur are blocked; maps, routes and the project's own photos stay open

policies.notes:
Written from the binary. It is a Capacitor application with a MapLibre map, so its code is the JavaScript in assets/public. What it needs: israelhiking.osm.org.il (its own API, tiles and uploaded photos), api.openstreetmap.org and overpass-api.de (map data), upload.wikimedia.org and commons.wikimedia.org (point of interest photos), inature.info, and RevenueCat (api.revenuecat.com and its siblings) for the subscription.

Blocked: Google Tag Manager and Analytics; YouTube, which is an embedded help video (youtube.com/embed); Facebook, which is the project's group page and a share link; and imgur, which is where some user photos are hosted and where uploads went, so those photos do not load and an upload to imgur fails. The embedded video's stream comes from googlevideo.com hosts that cannot be listed one by one; blocking www.youtube.com stops the embed before it asks for them.

What this does not block: photos on Wikimedia and on the project's own server, which are most of them. That is why the catalog entry carries hasUnmodestImage. Not yet watched on a device through the tunnel.

What it needs: api-prod.startach.io, api-yedidim.startach.io, yedidim.startach.io, redirect.startach.io, platform.startach.org.il, Google Maps, Firebase and Sentry. networkPolicy.desc: Its station data, the map tiles and its Firebase sign in, and nothing else

policies.notes:
An allow list, written from the binary. It is a Flutter application, so its own code is in lib/arm64-v8a/libapp.so in the ABI split, which tools/extract_hosts.py does not read; the strings there were read by hand.

What it dials: docs.google.com, where the station list is a Google Sheet (gviz/tq?tqx=out:json) and reports go to two Google Forms (formResponse); tile.openstreetmap.org for the map; Firestore, and Firebase Auth with Google sign in and reCAPTCHA (identitytoolkit, securetoken, firebaseinstallations, www.googleapis.com, accounts.google.com, www.recaptcha.net, www.gstatic.com/recaptcha). www.google.com is asked for its favicon, which reads as a connectivity check.

Not dialled: waze.com/ul and google.com/maps/dir are links handed to the navigation apps. The base APK also carries dozens of github.com hosts and YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Twitch, LinkedIn and X: library resources, never used. No ads, no analytics, no Crashlytics were found.

Not yet watched on a device through the tunnel: a host built at runtime would show up there as WHITELIST_MISS.
